method: An 802.1Q VLAN identifier is 12 bits, so IDs run from 1 to 4094: 0 and 4095 are reserved for priority-tagged frames, and 1002 to 1005 are reserved for legacy Token Ring and FDDI VLANs. The planner works in the inclusive range you enter, between 1 and 4094. It counts the usable IDs as the range width minus any of 1002 to 1005 that fall inside it, subtracts the distinct in-use IDs that are inside the range and not reserved, and refuses the plan when fewer IDs are free than you asked for. The in-use field accepts space- or comma-separated single IDs and inclusive ranges such as 20 or 30-39; reversed ranges, non-numeric tokens and IDs above 4095 are refused, and IDs outside the range or in the reserved block are counted as ignored. The plan takes the lowest free IDs in ascending order, up to 32 of them, so it is contiguous whenever the free space allows; the number of contiguous blocks the allocation spans and the largest remaining free block are reported so a fragmented result is visible. Each allocated ID is also shown as a 16-bit tag control field, PCP x 8192 + DEI x 4096 + VLAN ID, with the priority code point and drop-eligible bit you choose, which is the value you would match in a packet capture or a switch debug trace. Limits: 1 to 32 VLANs per plan, at most 128 in-use entries or ranges, whole-number IDs only. The planner does not read any switch configuration, does not know which VLANs exist on trunk or access ports, and does not model provider-reserved or private VLAN ranges, so the result is a suggestion to check before applying. The calculation runs entirely in the browser with no storage, uploads or network access.

sources.title: IEEE 802.1Q carries a 12-bit VLAN identifier: 0 and 4095 are reserved, leaving 1 to 4094 as usable VLAN IDs.
VLAN IDs 1002 to 1005 are reserved for legacy Token Ring and FDDI VLANs and are not available for ordinary Ethernet VLANs.
The tag control information field packs a 3-bit priority code point, a drop-eligible indicator and the 12-bit VLAN ID, so its value is PCP x 8192 + DEI x 4096 + VLAN ID.
VLAN 1 is the default VLAN on most switches and is normally carried untagged on access ports.
